_meta.what: The trigger watch: named people and events the desk should act on — executives leaving or joining companies that sponsor F1 / Formula E, new CEOs and marketing / commercial owners at companies in the ICP, and pre-IPO, listing and M&A moments at tech and blockchain names that fit the grid. Each row carries the ICP judgment, the series fit, the action and the sources. Filled by the desk (operator, 11 Sep 2026: 'you need to decide if they are our ICP … you need to do this proactively').
_meta.how: Live sweep on 11 Sep 2026 from press releases, SEC filings and Tier-1 trade press via search summaries (many primary domains are egress-blocked in the desk's sandbox — treat VERIFIED as 'verify the link before circulation'). Actions: start_sequence (open the outreach sequence for this trigger type), sponsor_side (an existing partner's people moved — a renewal or activation conversation, not a cold pitch), watch (not yet actionable: in transition, outside the 90-day window, or the capital event has not completed), screen_out (not the ICP).

items.sponsor_link: none found on the grid; crypto exchanges (OKX, Crypto.com, Kraken, Bybit) are the precedent for blockchain brands on F1 cars
items.icp: YES, F1 only — build the case. $1B at a $21B post-money led by 1789 Capital (31 Aug 2026), up 40% from $15B in April; 1789 puts in ~$300M for a ~$500M combined stake. Proven sports buyer at scale: NHL league-wide prediction-market partner (Oct 2025), NY Rangers (Jan 2026), MLB exclusive Official Prediction Market Exchange (Mar 2026), LeBron James teasing a deal (5 Sep 2026). F1 whitespace is specific: Polymarket already runs ~500 active F1 markets and a dedicated F1 section but is not an F1 partner, and F1 has no prediction-market partner — MLB's precedent shows the category is treated as separate from sportsbooks.
items.team_lane: Betting / prediction lane. CLEAR THE RIGHTSHOLDER FIRST: F1 sold betting-operator rights centrally — Betway (Mar 2026, Europe/MENA/Canada/Mexico) and FanDuel (Apr 2026, US) — so a team-level prediction-market deal is a FOM clearance question before it is a sales question. Conflicted teams: Williams (Betway AND Jackpot City Casino), Alpine (Modo Casino), Audi (Stake, departed within 12 months). FE is a poor fit — a gambling-adjacent brand against FE's sustainability positioning, and no volume driver.
items.window_note: CONFIRMED on Bloomberg 31 Aug 2026 (the CryptoRank report alone was not enough). 15 days old. Two fresher events strengthen it: a marketing overhaul and senior executive hires on 11 Aug 2026 (CNBC) under Chief Growth Officer Travis VanderZanden, founder of Bird and ex-Uber/Lyft, who owns marketing; and Warren Jenson named CFO on 13 Sep 2026 as US and global expansion accelerates — a pre-IPO shape of hire.
risks: Rightsholder conflict: FOM has already sold betting-operator exclusivity to Betway and FanDuel. Establish whether a prediction market is a separable category in F1's contracts before approaching any team.

Political and regulatory exposure: 1789 Capital, co-founded by Donald Trump Jr., leads the round, and a House Oversight Committee letter addressed to CEO Shayne Coplan is dated 22 May 2026. A team board will raise both.
Regulatory patchwork across a 24-round calendar — legality of event contracts differs by race market.

items.from_company: Zscaler (prior: Twilio, Genesys, Wrike, Arm, Google, Microsoft)
items.sponsor_link: none found; leadership ties none found after checking Kim and CEO Sumit Dhawan
items.icp: F1 yes, but NOT NOW. Thoma Bravo took Proofpoint private in 2021 ($12.3B); >$2B ARR growing ~20%; Hornetsecurity acquired for $1.8B (completed Dec 2025, ~$200M ARR). CEO Dhawan has said since Oct 2024 that an IPO is the plan and, at Protect in Sep 2025, that 'the market is ready, in the near future' — but no filing has surfaced, and the only event inside the 90-day window is the July 2026 Goldman-led amend-and-extend pushing $5B+ of term loans from Aug 2028 to Aug 2030 after a tough process (about 40 lender amendments, AI concerns). Extending debt to 2030 is the shape of a company staying private, not listing. The CMO trigger (Kim, 1 Dec 2025) is 9.5 months old. No capital-plus-identity inflection today.
items.series_fit: F1 first. The buyer is the CISO, and enterprise-security brands sit in F1 for that reason (CrowdStrike, Bitdefender, Keeper, 1Password, Okta, Rubrik, Cato, SEALSQ); FE's audience is younger, urban and consumer-leaning. FE is not nothing: Hornetsecurity (Hannover; pan-European MSP/SMB) is a European brand-build problem and FE races in Berlin, Monaco, London and Madrid — if an S-1 lands and the company wants a $2-8M European play alongside the listing story, look at Lola (Silverstone, in-house from S13, no title partner, open cyber lane) or Porsche's unnamed second factory team if it carries its own roster. Cato Networks holds the cyber lane at Porsche's first team. Second call, not the first. Checked 15 Sep 2026.
items.team_lane: Cybersecurity is the most-sold tech lane on the F1 grid; the open teams are TGR Haas and Cadillac (N° 154 Horizon3 points at Cadillac). Direct rival Abnormal AI is parked on the same stale-trigger grounds.
items.window_note: Re-open the day an S-1 or a confidential-filing report appears, or a pre-IPO round prices. The July refinancing is inside the window but is the wrong kind of event.

Leadership: Uberti CEO, Zhu co-founder, Wachen co-founder and COO, Mark Rose CTO, VPs of production/platform/software/ASIC — no marketing or commercial executive, so the decision-maker is the CEO with Wachen as the operating path. items.icp: NOT a sponsor case — a rights-holder relationship. Capacity is the problem: privately held by Access Industries (Blavatnik, more than $7B invested), a ~$1B SURJ/PIF minority stake (Feb 2025), FY2024 revenue above $3B with a $936M loss, profitability targeted for 2026. Honest pillars: timing 17 (a reshuffle one day old), capacity 9, brand fit 14 (media has team-level precedent: CNBC at McLaren, TikTok and the FT at Aston Martin), urgency 12, ops fit 10 (content distribution is a real workstream) = 62. The reshuffle itself is the signal: Knappy as CMO & Customer Officer; Patrick Delany (ex-Foxtel) COO; Alex Gersh (ex-Sportradar CFO who led its Nasdaq listing) CFO — the shape of a listing; Darren Waterman moved to a new Chief Business Officer role for strategic partnerships, commercial development and corporate transactions.
items.series_fit: F1 over FE: DAZN's motorsport asset is Iberian F1 through 2030 with the Madrid GP; Disney+ takes Formula E's global streaming from Season 13, so DAZN's FE footprint is regional and may shrink.
items.team_lane: If ever pursued as a team media partner the asset is a Spanish driver — Williams (Sainz; no media partner on the roster) or Aston Martin (Alonso; TikTok and the Financial Times crowd the media lane). Otherwise the door is Waterman's partnerships remit, not a sponsorship sale.
items.window_note: Open a relationship with Knappy and Waterman on the Spain/Madrid story; re-score if DAZN files to list or if a team-level media deal appears anywhere on the grid.
